newsitem.title: FRANCE: France starts mine expropriation process - Eramet.
newsitem.headline: France starts mine expropriation process - Eramet.

text.p: French nickel producer Eramet said on Wednesday the French government had started a prodedure to take away the firm's nickel mining licence for Koniambo in New Caledonia.
Eramet received a letter from the government initiating the process on March 24, a company spokesman said.
"We now have one month to comment on the fact that we have not operated the mine for 10 years," he said.
In February the government, which owns 55 percent of Eramet, said it wanted to hand the concession to local Kanak interests, stating that Eramet had not exploited the mine since 1975.
Koniambo mining reserves would be used to supply a nickel smelter that Canadian group Falconbridge and local Kanak independence groups plan to build in the north of the island.
The smelter project is seen as a concession to Kanaks ahead of the 1998 referendum on independence for the French overseas territory.

The government came up with the plan to take away the Koniambo licence after talks between Eramet's Societe Le Nickel (SLN) and Kanak Societe Miniere du Sud Pacifique (SMSP) over an asset swap failed.
Eramet has said it would use all legal means in its possession to prevent the licence withdrawal, arguing it was unjustified and would affect its financial outlook.
Eramet puts the value of the Koniambo mine at between one and two billion francs, the spokesman said.
The figures were derived from estimates of cash flow generated over the potential life of the mine but may vary depending on nickel prices and other factors, he said.
Because the licence was given freely Eramet would not get compensation for its loss but the government has said it plans to start separate talks over compensation.
Eramet also owns the Thiebaghi mines in New Caledonia, which are crucial to its plans to produce over 60,000 tonnes of nickel by the year 2000 from a 1996 output of 56,000 tonnes.
